qa_pairs.question: What job parameters can a user configure when submitting an interactive application through Open OnDemand?
qa_pairs.answer: When submitting an interactive application through Open OnDemand, users can configure parameters such as the length of the job in hours, the number of cores, the amount of memory to allocate (in GB), and GPU resources. Currently, only the 'h100_1.10' Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) profile is available, which provides 10GB of memory and 1/8 of the compute power of a full NVIDIA H100 GPU. Users also have the option to be notified by email when their job starts.

qa_pairs.question: How can a user manage their interactive jobs and access their running applications in Open OnDemand?
qa_pairs.answer: After submitting an interactive job, users are directed to the 'My Interactive Sessions' page, where they can monitor the job's status (queued, running, or completed). Once a job is running, they can click the 'Connect to ...' button to launch the application in a new browser tab. For terminal access to the node running the application, users can click the button next to 'Host' that starts with `>_`. To terminate a job, they can click the red 'Delete' button in the job panel on the 'My Interactive Sessions' page.

qa_pairs.question: What interactive applications are currently supported on the Open OnDemand platform, and how can users request new application installations?
qa_pairs.answer: The Open OnDemand platform currently supports interactive applications including JupyterLab/Notebook, Rstudio, VSCode, Trillium Desktop, ParaView, Forge DDT/MAP, MATLAB, Ovito, SAS, Stata, and Open Composer. Users who wish to have an additional application installed should email support@scinet.utoronto.ca.
